title: Near-Exact Length Slack for Planar Directed Steiner Tree and Steiner Forest
summary: New LP-competitive planar network-design algorithms achieve polylogarithmic cost approximations with 1+ε path-length slack for directed Steiner tree and undirected Steiner forest. A complementary hardness result separates planar instances from general graphs.

results.title: A Little Length Slack Goes a Long Way in Planar Length-Constrained Network Design
results.summary: Planar length-constrained directed Steiner tree and undirected Steiner forest admit LP-competitive polylogarithmic approximations with arbitrarily small multiplicative length slack.
results.aiUse: The authors state that they first found weaker LP-competitive algorithms without AI assistance, then GPT-6 Astra improved the directed Steiner tree approximation to O(log² k/ε), supplied flow preprocessing and threshold arguments for Steiner forest, and suggested a median trick for length slack. The authors simplified and wrote the proofs, used the model for proofreading and figures, and state that they verified the results themselves.
results.body:
Consider a planar graph with nonnegative integral edge costs $c$ and lengths $\ell$, a length budget $h$, and $k$ connectivity demands. A bicriteria $(\alpha,\beta)$ approximation purchases a subgraph costing at most $\alpha$ times the optimum under the original budget $h$, while permitting demand paths of length at most $\beta h$. Hershkowitz, Huang, Jain, and Korimilli obtain polynomial-time, LP-competitive $O(\log^2 k/\varepsilon)$ approximation for length-constrained **directed Steiner tree** (LC-DST) with slack $1+\varepsilon$, and LP-competitive $O(\log^5 k/\varepsilon^2)$ approximation for undirected **Steiner forest** (LC-SF), again with slack $1+\varepsilon$. Their reduction also yields an $O(\log^6 k/\varepsilon)$ approximation for directed Steiner forest (LC-DSF) with slack $6+\varepsilon$. Running times are polynomial in $n$ and $1/\varepsilon$ for $0<\varepsilon<1$. The LP-competitive guarantee compares cost to a fractional relaxation, not merely the integral optimum.

Previously, Chekuri and Jain (APPROX/RANDOM 2026) obtained an LP-competitive $O(\log^2 k)$ approximation for planar LC-DST but with $O(\log k)$ length slack; their planar directed-forest approximation had $O(\log^6 k)$ cost factor and $O(\log k)$ slack without LP competitiveness. Hershkowitz and Huang had achieved $1+\varepsilon$ slack for the undirected single-root Steiner-tree problem, with LP-competitive cost $O(\log^3 k/\varepsilon)$. Thus the new directed and multicommodity guarantees remove a logarithmic multiplicative violation of the length budget, rather than merely improving constants.

For LC-DST, the algorithm recursively constructs a hierarchy of planar shortest-path separators under a mixture metric combining edge cost and length. Traditional separator recursion incurs additional length at each of $O(\log k)$ levels. Earlier shortcut schemes subdivided separators into predetermined pieces, but directed paths cannot necessarily travel backward from a shortcut's entry point. Instead, the algorithm scans each directed separator and greedily buys a candidate shortcut from the parent separator precisely when its mixture-metric route improves on continuation from the preceding shortcut. The purchases themselves induce variable-length, directionally reachable pieces. A two-way charging argument bounds shortcut cost by the cumulative reduction in solution-path length, and bounds extra path length by the fractional cost of canonical root-to-terminal paths. Appropriate mixture coefficients keep the latter excess below $\varepsilon h$.

For LC-SF, the authors adapt junction-tree decomposition to fractional rather than integral solutions. They bucket LP flow paths, intersect them with short separator chunks, and create rooted candidate subgraphs using the single-root algorithm. Dummy terminal edges encode the two portions of a pair's length allowance, selected through a flow-weighted median. Enumerating geometric flow thresholds prevents the cost of spreading a pair's fractional flow across many chunks from being paid repeatedly. A weighted averaging argument guarantees a low-density candidate, and greedy coverage of the remaining pairs supplies the logarithmic set-cover factor. The directed-forest guarantee follows through an earlier reduction.

The paper also gives a contrasting hardness boundary: assuming $\mathsf{NP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BPTIME}(2^{\mathrm{polylog}(n)})$, general-graph LC-SF has no polynomial-time $2^{\log^{1-\delta}k}$ approximation with slack below $3$, for fixed $\delta>0$; the corresponding LC-DSF hardness applies for any fixed positive slack. This emphasizes the role of planarity. The results remain bicriteria, and the directed multicommodity slack is $6+\varepsilon$, not $1+\varepsilon$. This is arXiv v1, a preprint without a reported proof-assistant formalization or completed peer review; the authors say they checked the arguments, which is not independent verification.
